content.title: About
content.content: Pork belly with skin is a thick cut of meat taken from the underside of a pig. In its raw state it is rich in fat, protein and connective tissue. The belly is widely used for roasting, braising, frying and smoking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pork belly is one of the fattiest pork cuts, making it ideal for juicy dishes.
The skin contains collagen that turns into a gelatinous texture during slow cooking.
In traditional Chinese cuisine the belly is often marinated in soy sauce and spices before roasting.
In the United States pork belly is the primary source of bacon.
Pork belly can be used to make bone‑rich broths high in gelatin.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Pork belly provides high‑quality animal protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies B1, B2, B3, B6 and B12, which support energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Source of zinc and iron
items.content: These minerals are important for immune health and oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Collagen in the skin
items.content: Collagen may contribute to joint and skin health when the meat is cooked slowly.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: The high fat content provides a long‑lasting feeling of satiety and a quick energy source.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Abundant saturated fat can raise cholesterol levels if consumed frequently.

items.title: Risk of foodborne pathogens
items.content: Raw pork belly may harbor bacteria such as Salmonella or parasites like Trichinella; thorough cooking is required.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pork.

items.title: Sodium in processed versions
items.content: Cured or smoked belly often contains added salt, which is a concern for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The belly can be roasted whole, cut into strips for frying, braised in soups, or cooked in a slow cooker. The skin is often left on for a crispy crackling or removed for leaner preparations. Marinades of soy sauce, honey, spices and herbs enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh pork belly in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in an airtight container for 3‑5 days. For longer storage freeze it in a sealed bag at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw in the fridge, not at room temperature, before cooking.
